Theorem 1.1: The exponent 2 + epsilon on the right-hand side of inequality (3) in Theorem 1.1 is incorrect for general q. With q distinct points a_j plus infinity, the product involves q + 1 terms, and the left-hand side scales roughly as H_{*,
u}(x)^{-(q+1)} over all valuations. For any q >= 2, we have q + 1 > 2 + epsilon, which implies that inequality (3) would hold for all sufficiently large x
